work.objective: Review rkendel1/appboundry for an unresolved reliability defect in packages/appboundry-host (the artifact host: guest execution and limits, collections and transactions, identity and sessions, backups, the capability ledger). The after-commit outbox (performOutbox, recoverOutbox, retryOutbox) is already tracked in issue #99; look elsewhere. Find one defect you can prove with a failing test.

findings.title: Admin session operations fail with QUERY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED once the sessions collection holds more than 1,000 records
findings.summary: The admin module reads the whole sessions collection with an unpaged FeltDB find() (`#sessions()` in admin.ts). FeltDB refuses an unpaged find() that matches more than 1,000 records (QUERY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED). The rest of the host already routes whole-collection reads through paged-read.ts because of this limit, but admin.ts does not. Once more than 1,000 sessions exist, every admin path that calls `#sessions()` throws instead of answering: listSessions, revokeSessions, disableUser's session revocation, and bootstrap --recover's operator-session revocation. Sessions are never pruned elsewhere, because only listSessions deletes expired ones and it fails first. So the condition is permanent. An operator can then no longer revoke a user's or a leaked token's access, and cannot recover operator access. The test admin-many-sessions.test.ts issues 1,005 sessions for one user and expects revokeSessions({ user }) to revoke 1,005. It received the error string 'threw QUERY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED ... find() on "_appboundry_sessions" matches more than 1000 records', so the test failed on its assertion. The same unpaged pattern affects operators, users and the audit log (admin.ts lines 95, 177, 268, 275).
findings.fix: Read the admin collections in pages with paged-read.ts's readAll, as backup.ts and collections.ts already do. For example, `#sessions()` becomes `readAll(this.#db, { collection: SESSIONS_COLLECTION })`; apply the same to `#operators()`, the users reads and audit(). Revocations that delete more sessions than one transaction allows should be split into batches.

finding.title: Admin session operations fail with QUERY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED once the sessions collection holds more than 1,000 records

The rest of the host already routes whole-collection reads through paged-read.ts because of this limit, but admin.ts does not. Once more than 1,000 sessions exist, every admin path that calls `#sessions()` throws instead of answering: listSessions, revokeSessions, disableUser's session revocation, and bootstrap --recover's operator-session revocation. Sessions are never pruned elsewhere, because only listSessions deletes expired ones and it fails first. So the condition is permanent. An operator can then no longer revoke a user's or a leaked token's access, and cannot recover operator access. The test admin-many-sessions.test.ts issues 1,005 sessions for one user and expects revokeSessions({ user }) to revoke 1,005. It received the error string 'threw QUERY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED ... find() on "_appboundry_sessions" matches more than 1000 records', so the test failed on its assertion. The same unpaged pattern affects operators, users and the audit log (admin.ts lines 95, 177, 268, 275).

For example, `#sessions()` becomes `readAll(this.#db, { collection: SESSIONS_COLLECTION })`; apply the same to `#operators()`, the users reads and audit().
